title: Poland puts AI to work guarding its border with Belarus
key_facts: Poland’s military and Border Guard are using an AI system called Inteligentna Granica (Intelligent Border) to watch the Belarus border, per Poland’s Operational Command.
It pulls feeds from cameras, drones and other sensors into one picture and flags activity that needs a human’s attention.
It is being tested on a stretch of the eastern border several dozen kilometres long; the trial also covers robotics and autonomous systems, which the command did not name.
It was built by the Artificial Intelligence Implementation Center of Poland’s Cyberspace Defense Forces together with the Border Guard.
The aim is to cut hours soldiers and border officers spend watching video and to speed the response to crossing attempts.
Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said in July the system would enter operational use in August.
It runs inside Operation Safe Podlasie, begun on 1 Aug 2024; about 5,000 troops support the Border Guard on the Belarus border each day.
quote_evidence: The system is being tested on a stretch of the eastern border several dozen kilometers long.
The software recognizes objects, assesses what they are doing and points operators to events that need attention, the cyber command said in July.
Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said in July that the system would enter operational use in August.
why_it_matters_hint: Poland is automating part of its Belarus border watch, with AI flagging events for human operators.
